title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Managing the Process - Opening
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: At exactly 2:00 PM, a procurement officer commences the public bid opening for an IFB. What actions are typically performed during this event?
options: The proposals are read aloud, evaluated for technical merit, and awarded immediately
The name of each bidder and their total submitted price are read aloud to the public, and a bid tabulation is created
The procurement officer negotiates the prices downward in front of the audience
Vendors are allowed to alter their pricing based on what the first vendor bid
questions.explain: A public bid opening is an administrative function of transparency where bids are unsealed, and the vendor names and bid amounts are read aloud and recorded on a tabulation sheet. No evaluation or award occurs at the opening.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If an agency discovers a significant error in the solicitation document on the morning of the bid opening, the most appropriate ethical and legal action is to:
options: Proceed with the opening and fix the error later during contract negotiation
Open the bids privately, fix the error, and ask vendors to re-price secretly
Formally postpone the bid opening via an urgent addendum to allow time to correct the error and give vendors a chance to adjust their bids
Award to the vendor who noticed the error first
questions.explain: If a critical error is found before opening, the process must be paused. The opening should be officially postponed (extended) to issue a corrective addendum, ensuring all vendors bid on accurate, fair specifications.

questions.q: How does a public opening for an RFP (Request for Proposals) generally differ from a public opening for an IFB (Invitation for Bids)?
options: RFP openings do not happen at all
Only the names of the proposers are read aloud at an RFP opening to protect trade secrets and negotiations; prices are usually kept confidential until notice of award
RFP openings require the vendors to read their own proposals aloud
There is no difference; prices and technical approaches are read aloud for both
questions.explain: Because RFPs involve subjective evaluations, trade secrets, and eventual negotiations, typically only the names of the submitting vendors are read aloud at the closing. Prices and proposal details are shielded from competitors until the evaluation/negotiation phase concludes.
